guide_enrichment.narrative: We are not treating Syracuse’s 66-3 opener or California’s 45-24 loss as proof of what happens next. The useful takeaway is that Syracuse showed balance and disruption, producing 513 total yards without a turnover while holding New Hampshire to 159 yards with five sacks and three takeaways. That profile helps explain why our numbers are more favorable to Syracuse than the market is.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Syracuse’s rushing offense against California’s front. California allowed 277 rushing yards to UCLA, while Syracuse ran for 238 yards in its opener and is expected to add Ahmad Miller and Ju’Juan Johnson to the backfield rotation. That matters because our matchup metrics identify California’s pass defense as the strongest obstacle for Syracuse.

recent_game.fact: Syracuse opened the 2026 season with a 66-3 home win over New Hampshire.
Syracuse scored 41 first-half points against New Hampshire, its most in a half during Fran Brown's tenure.
Ten Syracuse players recorded a reception and five players scored a rushing or receiving touchdown against New Hampshire.
Syracuse held New Hampshire to three points and 159 total yards while recording five sacks, nine tackles for loss and three takeaways.

opponent_notes.fact: California opened the season with a 45-24 home loss to UCLA.
California allowed 277 rushing yards and 184 passing yards against UCLA.
California produced 410 total yards against UCLA, including 291 passing yards and 119 rushing yards.
California running back A. Mohammed carried 28 times for 120 yards and one touchdown in the opener.

California's leading receivers in the opener were I. Strong with five catches for 94 yards, C. Hendricks with six catches for 66 yards and a touchdown, and M. Mason with four catches for 58 yards and a touchdown.

quarterback.fact: Syracuse quarterback Steve Angeli returned from his 2025 season-ending injury and passed for 263 yards against New Hampshire.
Angeli has passed for at least 230 yards in six consecutive games and has never thrown for fewer than 245 yards in a Syracuse appearance.
Angeli has completed 176 of 265 career passes for 2,352 yards, 23 touchdowns and three interceptions across Notre Dame and Syracuse.
California quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed 24 of 41 passes for 271 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions against UCLA.
Sagapolutele led the ACC with 24.31 completions per game as a freshman in 2025.

offensive_personnel.fact: Transfer running backs Ahmad Miller and Ju'Juan Johnson did not play against New Hampshire and are expected to make their Syracuse debuts against California.
Miller transferred from Jackson State after leading the SWAC with 1,054 rushing yards and adding nine touchdowns in 2025.
Johnson transferred from LSU after appearing in all 13 games in 2025 and recording at least one carry in every game.
True freshman Shavane Anderson Jr. rushed 10 times for 102 yards and three touchdowns in his collegiate debut against New Hampshire.
Running back Tylik Hill made his first career start and rushed 16 times for 91 yards and his first collegiate touchdown against New Hampshire.
Wide receiver Umari Hatcher set career highs with eight receptions, 147 yards and two touchdowns in the opener.
Tight end David Clement caught two passes for a career-high 35 yards, including his first collegiate touchdown on a 27-yard reception.
Transfer wide receiver Cole Weaver caught three passes for 32 yards in his Syracuse debut against New Hampshire.
Syracuse's projected offensive line is Trevion Mack at left tackle, Oluwafunto Akinshilo at left guard, Joe Cruz at center, Byron Washington at right guard and Kam Pringle at right tackle.
Syracuse's offensive line received an 87.0 pass-blocking grade from PFF against New Hampshire, second among ACC teams through Saturday's games.
Center Joe Cruz has appeared in 38 games with 17 starts and has allowed one sack in 657 pass-blocking opportunities, according to PFF.
Oluwafunto Akinshilo made his first career start at guard against New Hampshire.

defensive_personnel.fact: Four of Syracuse's five sacks against New Hampshire were recorded by transfers.
Transfer Keyshawn Johnson recorded 2.5 sacks, four tackles and a forced fumble in his Syracuse debut.
Transfer defensive lineman Tunmise Adeleye tied his career high with six tackles and recorded a sack in his Syracuse debut.
Transfer defensive lineman Jartavius Flounoy recorded four tackles, a half-tackle for loss and a forced fumble in his Syracuse debut.
Defensive lineman Rashard Perry recorded three tackles and his first career interception against New Hampshire.
Cornerback Chris Peal allowed 14 receiving yards when targeted and led Syracuse with four solo tackles against New Hampshire, according to PFF.

coaching_changes.fact: Vince Kehres is in his first season as Syracuse's defensive coordinator.

Syracuse also has first-year assistants John Scott Jr. as assistant head coach, co-defensive coordinator and defensive line coach; Perry Eliano as defensive backs coach; Jeremy Hawkins as edge coach; Marcus Walker as nickels coach; and Juan Castillo as offensive line coach.
Tosh Lupoi is in his first season as California's head coach and will coach his first road game in that role at Syracuse.

California's play callers are all in their first season with the program: offensive coordinator Jordan Somerville, co-offensive coordinator Ike Hilliard, defensive coordinator Michael Hutchings and co-defensive coordinator Da'Von Brown.

injury_availability.fact: Steve Angeli returned against New Hampshire after suffering a season-ending injury in the fourth game of the 2025 season.
Umari Hatcher played in the season opener after missing the entire 2025 season due to injury.
Freshman wide receiver Calvin Russell III is expected to return to the field in October.
Defensive lineman Rashard Perry returned in the opener after a season-ending injury limited him to five games in 2025.

offensive_context.fact: Syracuse recorded 238 rushing yards and 275 passing yards against New Hampshire.
Syracuse converted 66.7 percent of its third downs and recorded 32 first downs in the opener.
Syracuse did not commit a turnover against New Hampshire.
Syracuse had 10 different players catch a pass in Week 1.
In offensive coordinator Jeff Nixon's last 18 games with his Week 1 starting quarterback available, Syracuse is 14-4 while averaging 471.4 yards and 36.8 points per game.

defensive_context.fact: Syracuse allowed 60 rushing yards and 99 passing yards against New Hampshire.
Twenty-four Syracuse defenders recorded a tackle against New Hampshire, including 20 with multiple tackles.
Nine different Syracuse players recorded at least a half-tackle for loss in the opener.
Syracuse's five sacks against New Hampshire were its second-highest single-game total under Fran Brown.

special_teams.fact: Davien Kerr blocked a New Hampshire punt that went out of the end zone for a safety.
Kerr also returned two punts for 50 yards against New Hampshire.
Demetres Samuel Jr. returned four punts for 83 yards, an average of 20.8 yards per return, and added a 42-yard return of a safety kick.
Kicker Tripp Woody made a 34-yard field goal in the opener and is 11-for-11 on career attempts inside 40 yards.
Freshman Jimmy Gregg is Syracuse's projected punter and punted twice in his collegiate debut against New Hampshire.

series_context.fact: Syracuse leads the all-time series with California 2-1 entering the fourth meeting.
Syracuse won the teams' first matchup as ACC opponents, 33-25 at California in 2024.
In the 2024 win, Syracuse scored on its first six possessions and made four field goals.
California's only previous trip to Syracuse was a 20-14 Orange win in 1967; this will be the Golden Bears' first game in the Dome.

other_relevant.fact: The Sept. 12 matchup is the ACC opener for both Syracuse and California.
Syracuse has won three of its last four ACC openers, including each of the previous two seasons.
Five Syracuse players made their first FBS starts against New Hampshire, including first-time starters Tylik Hill, Jimmy Gregg and Nissi Ogbebor.
